samples.summary: The "refuse rather than replicate a read-time truncation" guard lives only in `writeFullDocument`; every incremental writer happily writes the truncated model back, deleting a peer's rows
samples.evidence:
`writeFullDocument` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3330-3352) refuses a document containing a table at `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`, on the stated grounds that `getDocument()` truncated that table to `rows: []` and rewriting it would turn a read-time truncation into a replicated deletion. But the same truncated model reaches the CRDT through writers that carry no such refusal:
- `updateBlock` → `tree.editByPath(blockPath, endPath, buildBlockNode(block, this.blockPathNestingDepth(...)))` (~line 1750): if `block` is the table read at the cap, `buildBlockNode` is called with `depth >= MAX` and emits `children: []`, replacing the peer's rows in the tree with nothing.
- `updateTableCell` (~line 2924) → `buildCellNode(cell, rowDepth)` — same, for every nested table inside the rewritten cell.
- `insertTableRow` / `insertTableColumn` (~2841/2874) and `insertBlockAfter`/`insertBlocksAfter`.
- `setHeader` / `setFooter` tree paths (lines 968-985, 1007-1026) rewrite the whole header/footer node from `getDocument()`'s truncated blocks via `buildBlockNode(b, 0)` with no cap check at all.
So the refusal binds only the one path that already had no realistic caller, while the ordinary edit paths do exactly the destructive thing it was added to prevent. (Backend `writeDocsRoot` has the same guard and no incremental twin, so the hole is frontend-side.)

samples.summary: `assertValidBlock`'s new `depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` rejects the deepest *legal* document: any content block inside the outermost-permitted table chain 400s
samples.evidence: `depth` counts tables entered (incremented only at line 502 when descending into `tableData.rows[].cells[].blocks[]`). The writers/readers permit tables at depths `0 … MAX-1`, i.e. a chain of exactly MAX nested tables, whose innermost cell blocks therefore sit at depth == MAX. The new check fires on *any* block at depth MAX, table or not, so a document that `writeDocsRoot` accepts, `readDocsRoot` returns whole, and the DOCX importer deliberately produces (docx-importer.ts:435-440, test asserts `importedDepth === MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`) cannot be PUT back — breaking the GET→edit→PUT identity this file documents. The check should be `depth > MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`, or only apply to `type === 'table'` blocks.

samples.summary: `capTableNesting` returns early for `baseDepth <= 0`, so a paste at the top level is not capped at all
samples.evidence: `if (baseDepth <= 0) return blocks;` skips the whole recursion, so a fragment whose *own* nesting exceeds `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` pastes uncapped at document top level — exactly the "absolute invariant" the function's own doc comment claims to enforce ("Paste is a producer … so it owes the same absolute invariant"). Today it happens to be masked by the unrelated `MAX_TABLE_DEPTH = 8` sanitizer bound on the `WAFFLEDOCS_MIME` flavour (clipboard.ts:72/309), so the hole is latent, but any producer of `Block[]` reaching `insertBlocks` with deeper nesting (a future paste flavour, an import path) writes past the cap.

samples.summary: The sibling paste path `pasteTableCells` bypasses the new nesting cap entirely
samples.evidence: `executePastePlan` routes `plan.kind === 'tableCells'` to `this.pasteTableCells(plan.cells)` (line 1575), which never calls `capTableNesting` and never consults `doc.tableNestingDepth`. `pasteTableCells` (4698-…) writes each pasted `TableCell`'s `blocks` — which the clipboard sanitizer allows to contain up to 8 levels of nested tables (clipboard.ts:72) — into a cell at whatever depth the caret sits. Pasted into a cell near the ceiling this produces tables at depths >= MAX, which the writers then emit with no rows (silent loss of the pasted table) and which trip `writeFullDocument`'s refusal afterwards. Only `insertBlocks` got the guard.

samples.summary: The budgeted (possibly short) merge expansion is not paint-only: the same normalized rectangle drives cell-range delete and copy
samples.evidence: `normalizeCellRange` applies `MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS` unconditionally (line 213-215), and its output is what `Selection.getNormalizedRange` returns to *every* consumer — including the destructive cell-range clear in text-editor.ts:4169-4185 (which wipes `cell.blocks` for the whole rectangle) and the copy path `getSelectedTableCells` (text-editor.ts:4317). The doc comment for `MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS` asserts "It bounds `normalizeCellRange` and nothing else… Every other caller feeds the result to a write" — but this caller feeds a write too. On a table large enough to exhaust the budget the clear would slice through a merge, the precise corruption the unbounded default was kept for.

samples.summary: `insertBlocks` measures the target depth from a block that may not be in `blockParentMap` yet, silently disabling the paste cap
samples.evidence: `this.ensureEditableBlock(); const pos = this.cursor.position;` then `this.doc.tableNestingDepth(pos.blockId)`. `Doc.tableNestingDepth` (document.ts:158-170) reads `_blockParentMap`, which is populated at *layout* time; `ensureEditableBlock()` can split/create a block whose id has never been laid out, so the lookup misses and the depth answers 0 — `capTableNesting` then early-returns (clipboard.ts:430) and the paste is uncapped at a target that may in fact be deep inside a table.

samples.summary: The layout's nesting cap is off by one relative to the reader's
samples.evidence: `computeLayout` calls `computeTableLayout(..., nestingDepth default 0)` for a *top-level* table (layout.ts:510), and `computeTableLayout` passes that same value to `layoutCellBlocks` (line 285). So inside `layoutCellBlocks`, `nestingDepth` is the depth of the *enclosing* table, while the table block being examined is one deeper. The check `nestingDepth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` therefore truncates at model depth MAX+1, one level past where `treeNodeToBlock` truncates (depth MAX). Harmless (looser, not tighter) but it contradicts the comment claiming it mirrors the reader, and any future code that relies on the two agreeing would be wrong.

verdict.reason: Verified in the tree: `hasTableAtNestingCap` is referenced only inside `writeFullDocument` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3332-3334); no incremental writer consults it. `buildBlockNode` (:386-401) emits `children: []` at/past the cap while `treeNodeToBlock` (:517-535) reads the same table as `rows: []`, so any writer that replaces an existing subtree from a `getDocument()` model converts a read-time truncation into a replicated deletion of a peer's rows. Such replacing writers exist and carry no refusal: `updateBlock` (:1753-1757, editByPath over the block node), `updateTableCell` (:2934-2938, replaces the cell subtree, reached from merge-cells at packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:1155,1184), plus `insertTableRow`/`insertTableColumn` (:2843-2900). Worse, `setHeader` (:968-985) and `setFooter` (:1007-1026) take a tree path that bypasses `writeFullDocument` entirely and rebuild the whole header/footer node with `buildBlockNode(b, 0)` from the truncated model with no cap check; the refusal only applies on their treeless fallback (:960-966, :999-1005). The design doc (docs/design/docs/tables/docs-nested-tables.md:297-306) gives the same rationale for the refusal but exempts the incremental writers, which also rewrite reader-produced models. No guard elsewhere makes these unreachable — document.ts:925 and editor.ts:4232 only prevent *creating* new nesting past the cap, not rewriting an existing peer-written deep subtree. Data loss on replicated CRDT rows is squarely in the correctness lane; the pathological input needed affects likelihood, not whether the gap is real.

finding.summary: `buildRowNode`/`buildCellNode` called without the newly-required `depth` argument (3 sites)
finding.evidence: The delta changed `buildRowNode(row: TableRow, depth: number)` and `buildCellNode(cell: TableCell, depth: number)` to take a *required* second parameter, but three pre-existing call sites still pass one argument: `buildRowNode(row)` (line 2775, insertTableRow), `buildCellNode(cells[r])` (line 2818, insertTableColumn) and `buildCellNode(cell)` (line 2858, updateTableCell). Each is a TypeScript `TS2554: Expected 2 arguments, but got 1` — and packages/frontend runs no `tsc` at all, so nothing in CI catches it. At runtime `depth` is `undefined`, which propagates to `buildBlockNode(b, undefined)` and re-triggers the `depth = 0` default, so the nesting counter silently restarts at zero for every row insert, column insert and cell update: a nested table written through these paths is never capped at its true document depth.

verdict.reason: The claimed one-argument call sites do not exist in the source. A repo-wide grep for `buildRowNode|buildCellNode` returns exactly three call sites in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts, and all three pass the depth argument: line 2845 `buildRowNode(row, rowDepth)` (insertTableRow), line 2888 `buildCellNode(cells[r], rowDepth)` (insertTableColumn), line 2928 `buildCellNode(cell, rowDepth)` (updateTableCell). Each method first computes the depth via `resolveTableRowDepth(tableBlockId)` (defined at lines 2785-2794, returning `blockPathNestingDepth(path, region) + 1`), destructuring `{ path: tablePath, rowDepth }` at lines 2844, 2877 and 2927. The reviewer's cited lines hold unrelated code: 2775 is blank, 2818 is `let block: Block;` inside `resolveTableBlock`, 2858 is the closing brace of `insertTableRow`. The claimed runtime mechanism is also absent — `buildBlockNode(block: Block, depth: number)` at line 386 has a required parameter with no `depth = 0` default, so there is no "re-triggers the default" path. The only one-argument forms (`buildRowNode(row)`, `buildCellNode(cells[r])`, `buildCellNode(cell)`) appear in docs/tasks/archive/2026/03/20260329-table-granular-updates-todo.md lines 251/285/326, which is an archived markdown planning document, not compiled code. No TS2554 and no depth-counter reset exists.

finding.summary: The write-side nesting cap only holds for full-document writes; every incremental insert path restarts `depth` at 0
finding.evidence: `buildBlockNode`'s cap is relative to the `depth` its caller supplies, but all incremental writers call it with the default 0: `insertBlocksAfter` (2371), `replaceBlock`-style edit at 1723, 2312, 2335, 2505, 2584. A paste or block insert of an N-deep table into a cell that already sits at depth 31 therefore writes a chain of 31+N tables into the CRDT — precisely the "model deeper than any reader materializes" state the delta's importer cap and `writeFullDocument` refusal exist to prevent. Consequences are not a crash (the layout caps itself in table-layout.ts:145) but permanently invisible content and a document that every later `writeFullDocument`/`setHeader`-treeless call now *throws* on (the new guard at 3260), i.e. an unrepairable doc.

verdict.reason: The premise is not present in the code. `buildBlockNode` at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:386 declares `depth: number` as a REQUIRED parameter with no default (the comment at 375-381 says a default was deliberately removed for exactly this reason). Every incremental writer passes a computed nesting depth, not 0: `updateBlock` at 1756 (`blockPathNestingDepth(blockPath, region)`), `insertBlockAfter` at 2376, `insertBlocksAfter` (the paste path) at 2415-2416 (`siblingDepth`), `splitBlock` at 2499/2560/2646 (`blockDepth`), and the row/cell structural writers via `resolveTableRowDepth` at 2785-2794/2844-2845. `blockPathNestingDepth` (1663-1669) derives the count from the path's [row,cell,block] triplets region-aware. The only literal-0 call sites are genuinely depth-0 positions: `insertBlock` at a body top-level index (2347), `setHeader`/`setFooter` top-level region blocks (975, 1016), and `writeFullDocument` root children (3352/3355/3360). Therefore the described scenario — pasting into a cell at depth 31 writing a 31+N chain past MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH — cannot arise via these paths; the cap at line 398 binds incremental writes too. The reviewer's cited line numbers (1723, 2312, 2335, 2371, 2505, 2584) contain no `buildBlockNode` calls in this tree. The repo's own notes (docs/tasks/active/20260914-table-drag-merge-selection-lessons.md:36) record the `depth = 0` default as a prior state that was changed.
